concepts.clue: A four-letter plant word. It rhymes with “boot”.
concepts.text: Roots hold many plants in the soil. They take in water and minerals from the soil, helping the plant grow.
concepts.alt: A plant with branching roots below the soil. Arrows show water moving from soil into the roots.

concepts.clue: A four-letter plant word. It rhymes with “boss”.
concepts.text: Moss is a small plant without flowers. It often grows in damp, shady places and takes in water through its surface.
concepts.alt: Small moss plants form a green mat on a damp rock under shade. Water droplets reach the surface.

concepts.clue: A four-letter plant word. It rhymes with “gem”.
concepts.text: A stem supports a plant’s leaves and flowers. It carries water from the roots to other parts of the plant.
concepts.alt: A plant with its stem highlighted between roots and leaves. Upward arrows show water travelling through the stem.

baseline.stem: Which part of many plants takes in water from the soil?
A plant stays firmly in the soil on a windy day. Which part helps it stay in place?
Where would you most likely find moss growing?
Which part supports the leaves of a plant?
Water moves from roots towards leaves. Which part carries it between them?

post.stem: What is one job of a plant’s roots?
A seedling has damaged roots. What may become more difficult?
How does moss take in water?
A gardener wants a suitable place for moss. Which spot should they choose?
options: A dry windowsill in full sun
A moist rock under a tree
It supports leaves and carries water
It is always below the soil

post.stem: A flower has roots in water. How does water reach the flower above?
